title: The Suspicious Email
briefing: A finance coordinator at Acme Corp Test reported an urgent email asking employees to verify payroll credentials before a system freeze. Investigate the message, headers, and related records using simulated evidence only—do not visit external links or interact with live systems.
learning_objectives: Identify spoofing or lookalike domains in sender headers and display names.
Spot urgency-driven social engineering tactics and mismatched link destinations.
Distinguish relevant phishing clues from routine, unrelated workplace records.

content.subject: ACTION REQUIRED: Payroll Portal Locked in 2 Hours
content.body: Dear Team Member, due to an urgent security update, your payroll account will be suspended in 2 hours unless you confirm your password immediately at https://login.acm3-corp-support.example.com/payroll-verify

content.spf_result: fail (domain acm3-corp-support.example.com does not designate 203.0.113.88 as permitted sender)

content.summary: Scheduled HVAC maintenance on Floor 3 between 17:00 and 19:00 UTC.

decisions.prompt: How should this message be classified and handled?

options.label: Phishing attempt — quarantine the message, block the spoofed/lookalike domain and IP, and warn users not to enter credentials.
Legitimate IT notice — approve the sender and instruct employees to reset passwords via the link.
Harmless spam — archive the email with no further action or user notice.

decisions.feedback_correct: Correct. The lookalike domain ('acm3-corp-support.example.com'), failing SPF/DMARC checks, mismatched link target ('198.51.100.42'), and artificial 2-hour urgency are classic phishing indicators.
decisions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. Look closely at the sender address ('acm3-corp-support.example.com' vs. 'acme-corp.test'), SPF/DMARC failures, and the urgent credential request—those point to phishing rather than a legitimate notice or harmless spam.

hints.text: Start by checking whether the sender's identity, email authentication checks, and link destination match the organization's official domain.
Focus on the email content and message delivery headers rather than routine employee or facility records.
Inspect 'ev_email_01' and 'ev_headers_02'—specifically look at the '1' replaced with '3' in the domain, SPF/DMARC failures, and the raw IP link target.
Phishing often combines typosquatting/lookalike domains and artificial time pressure to trick users into handing over credentials on a deceptive page.

conclusion.prompt: Summarize your final investigation conclusion for 'The Suspicious Email'.
conclusion.model_summary: A simulated phishing email impersonating Acme IT Security used a lookalike domain ('acm3-corp-support.example.com'), failed SPF/DMARC checks, a mismatched IP link target, and urgent language to attempt credential theft.
